reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage as a network opportunity in which partner income is tied to community turnover and claims that participants became dollar millionaires within months. The speaker presents expanding earning opportunities, directs viewers to register through the contact information, and encourages participation rather than reporting on or critically examining the scheme.

citations.quote: The huge turnover of the Forsage community is the income of partners.
Some of the Forsage partners became dollar millonaires within a few months.
Contact me, I will explain in detail how to properly register.
now the opportunities for our partners are expanding more than ever.

opening.argument: The presentation acknowledges genuine uncertainty and operational difficulty rather than describing effortless or universal success. It identifies “extremely high gas prices” and says, “We have faced many challenges lately,” while also attributing criticism to alleged fakes and imitations. Those statements give viewers context about volatility, fees, and competing versions. The millionaire statement is limited to “Some” partners, not a promise that every viewer will profit. On the supplied evidence, the message can reasonably be read as an optimistic update with qualifications, not a guarantee of returns.

citations.quote: We have faced many challenges lately.
extremely high gas prices, due to which transactions fees on the Ethereum network have grown monstrously.
Some of the Forsage partners became dollar millonaires within a few months.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing reading treats a limited success claim as a promise to the audience. But “Some” does not mean all, and the discussion expressly identifies high transaction fees and recent challenges. Those qualifications undercut the claim that the speaker presents risk-free certainty. Even the criticism is characterized as involving fakes and copies, which is context about competing versions rather than proof that every statement here is deceptive.

citations.quote: We have faced many challenges lately.
transactions fees on the Ethereum network have grown monstrously.
Some of the Forsage partners became dollar millonaires within a few months.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging fees and challenges is not a meaningful risk warning when the overall message still emphasizes expanding opportunities and extraordinary earnings. The statement about millionaires supplies a powerful success implication without explaining likelihood, losses, eligibility, or conditions. “Some” limits grammar, but it does not make the earnings claim substantiated or non-promotional.

citations.quote: now the opportunities for our partners are expanding more than ever.
Some of the Forsage partners became dollar millonaires within a few months.

opening.argument: The material can be understood as an informational update about how a crypto community and its technical programs are changing. It discusses independence from a single blockchain, new programs called AX3 and AX4, additions to smart-contract functionality, and expansion of the Academy. The stated purpose is to explain updates and ecosystem structure, while the accompanying description says the speaker will explain how to register properly. That is consistent with an operational or technology-oriented presentation, even if it also expresses an optimistic view of participation.

citations.quote: We decided that we should be independent from any one blockchain, and this is another step towards maximum decentralization.
We are already launching updates programs AX3 and AX4
The Forsage Academy will also have new opportunities.
I will explain in detail how to properly register.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing argument assumes that discussing opportunities makes the entire presentation a solicitation. Yet the supplied speech spends substantial space on blockchain independence, smart contracts, programs, and community structure. Explaining how registration works can be operational guidance, and the evidence does not show the speaker demonstrating a payment, collecting credentials, or guaranteeing an outcome. The presentation therefore remains plausibly an update or tutorial about a crypto platform.

citations.quote: We decided that we should be independent from any one blockchain
additional programs will be added which have no analogs in smart contracts yet.
I will explain in detail how to properly register.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical vocabulary does not change the presentation's central appeal. The update language is repeatedly tied to partners' expanding opportunities, records, and earnings, while the description directs viewers toward registration. The material does not merely demonstrate code or explain blockchain concepts; it presents participation as a way to earn and promotes access to the program.

citations.quote: now the opportunities for our partners are expanding more than ever.
giving the participants the best opportunities to earn money.
Contact me, I will explain in detail how to properly register.

opening.argument: The supplied evidence describes a branded crypto service and a contact-based explanation of registration, which can be framed as ordinary promotion of access to a digital product or community. It does not identify a required deposit, request credentials, or show a guaranteed return. The sampled visuals show a presenter and the Forsage branding, including a closing logo, but no transaction interface or payment instruction. The text does mention community turnover and partner income, yet that alone does not establish the specific mechanics or outcome for any individual viewer.

citations.quote: Forsage io - now on TRX
Contact me, I will explain in detail how to properly register.
The huge turnover of the Forsage community is the income of partners.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence supports promotion of a named digital service, but promotion is not automatically proof of a scam mechanism. The speech does not specify a deposit amount, credential request, or guaranteed return, and the sampled closing frame is simply branding. “Community turnover” may describe an ecosystem's aggregate activity without proving how a particular viewer pays or receives money. The judge should not infer missing mechanics from the mere presence of registration language.

citations.quote: The huge turnover of the Forsage community is the income of partners.
Forsage io - now on TRX

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is not whether a deposit or password appears on a sampled frame. The speaker expressly says partner income comes from community turnover, describes partners earning money, and directs viewers to register. That is evidence of a network-based earning appeal, not ordinary retail commerce. The absence of a displayed payment screen does not negate the mechanism the speech itself describes.
